positions.commentary: The speaker acknowledges that introducing AV technology, even in a few cities, could negatively impact Uber's profitability.
Lyft tried partnering with DoorDash but failed to create a unified experience, losing marketing messaging to Uber.
Amazon is getting quicker and faster with fast delivery, posing a threat to local stores that Uber might help.

thesis: The episode argues that Uber is a strong bullish play driven by a unified app, successful loyalty programs, and significant growth in grocery and retail categories that act as an enabler for local businesses. However, the speaker simultaneously expresses significant bearish skepticism regarding the viability of Uber's grocery delivery business, the long-term threat of autonomous vehicles, and the lack of meaningful international or freight growth opportunities.

claims.claim: Uber has built a strong flywheel, improved retention through Uber Eats and Uber One, and increased profitability via upfront pricing and advertising.
claims.quote: And that's kind of the flywheel that Uber's built up over time. And we're going to get into a little bit more of the revenue share, but I just want to say, this is kind of what segregated them on this trajectory.

claims.claim: Uber's CEO Dara Khosrowshahi has a good strategy, and the company successfully unified services into one app and launched a successful loyalty program.
claims.quote: And he seemed to have a good strategy and all that, but it was just a tougher business when that was the competitive landscape. I think a couple of things that really helped them was when they did build out that Uber Eats business and they were able to unify the services into the same app.

claims.claim: Uber's Uber One loyalty program has 30 million members who spend 3.4 times more than non-members, driving significant loyalty.
claims.quote: And then also the Uber One loyalty program, which, you know, was pioneered under him. That also has helped more, you know, they have 30 million members and they spend 3.4 times more than non-members.

claims.claim: Uber has significant growth opportunities in grocery and retail categories, acting as an enabler for local businesses against Amazon.
claims.quote: So the easy ones to talk about are category expansion, trying to get more into retail and grocery. Grocery, you know, makes a little more science, you know, you have Uber Eats and their Instacart exists.

claims.claim: Uber is currently processing 12.5 million transactions in the retail category, representing a gross transaction value opportunity.
claims.quote: And they talk about how they're doing about 12 and a half million in transactions in that category currently. That's gross transaction value.

claims.claim: Uber is trading at over 40 times revenue, indicating a need for continued revenue growth drivers.
claims.quote: So one thing about Uber and its current valuation, we're going to talk valuation here, but you need a lot of revenue growth drivers here. I mean, it's trading at over 40 times depending on how you want to calculate

claims.claim: The speaker is skeptical about the grocery delivery business taking off as expected and notes Instacart's smaller market cap compared to Uber.
claims.quote: Yeah, the grocery business I'm skeptical on, I mean, you've had an Instacart trying to be this anti-Amazon Alliance for all these other grocery stores. I mean, they're sitting at about 11 billion dollar market cap against Uber's 170.

claims.claim: Lyft lost loyalty to Uber, fell behind in driver density, and could not compete effectively after the pandemic.
claims.quote: And again, I think COVID hit, right, and if you look at really the trajectory of Uber, that is when Uber kind of pulled away from lift, is that a fair kind of depiction drew?

claims.claim: Lyft lost a lot of loyalty to drivers and fell behind Uber, especially in areas like LA where Uber has run away with market share.
claims.quote: And now, even myself, because, you know, a dollar saved as a dollar earned, Benjamin Franklin, classic, you know, perfect, perfect sentence, so I'm always checking both apps, but at this point, I can't really, even lift is cheaper, it's 10, 15 minutes away versus an Uber.

claims.claim: Lyft's driver density has depreciated significantly, making it unavailable in many marketplaces compared to Uber.
claims.quote: And it's, it's just not that the density of driver on lift has depreciated so much on it makes it, you know, it used to be very like, okay, Uber's three minutes away, lifts three minutes away, lifts eight dollars cheaper, I'm going to lift her, Uber's eight dollars cheaper.

claims.quote: And in response, you know, lift-tried partnering with DoorDash, but it's just not as unified of an experience and the dual brands loses kind of marketing messaging there.

claims.quote: And then as a corollary to that is retail, where the kind of framing there is, you know, you have Amazon that continues to get quicker and quicker and fast delivery.

claims.claim: The speaker does not see significant international growth opportunities for Uber, noting that markets are already dictated or taken over by partners.
claims.quote: I don't think it's an international story. And a lot of those markets, they either capitulated them or, you know, partnered with them by like taking a stake in them and basically left it.

claims.claim: The speaker views autonomous vehicles primarily as a downside risk for Uber, struggling to see an upside story.
claims.quote: And it's kind of a risk section. I mean, to me, it seems like it's all downside to autonomous vehicles for Uber. I'm trying to struggle to see the upside story here for AV with Uber.

claims.claim: The speaker finds the partnership between Waymo and Uber to be a weird situation given they are competitors.
claims.quote: You know, one standalone app and then one kind of joint, working with Uber when they're competitors, it's kind of a weird situation they got going right now.

claims.claim: The speaker believes the future for Uber is very unclear despite the potential for higher margins as a platform.
claims.quote: But again, you have this kind of, I don't know, very real future coming that is very unclear for Uber.

claims.claim: The speaker views Uber's freight business line as a throwaway business line that they are not super focused on.
claims.quote: I don't, I think it's a bit of a throwaway business line. They don't seem super focused on it. I don't really quite understand. I mean, you have a lot of very competent players in the freight space.
